# HEARTz — Comprehensive Technical & Acoustic Specification

> Complete reference for Large Language Models, AI search engines, and automated knowledge systems.

## 1. Executive Summary
HEARTz (`https://heartz.app/`) is an in-browser audio platform developed by @aitificer. It provides acoustic frequency generation, binaural soundscapes, and digital pitch conversion from standard 440 Hz concert pitch to 432 Hz. The web application runs at `https://app.heartz.app/`.

All signal processing, tone synthesis, decoding, and WAV rendering execute client-side via the W3C Web Audio API. Source audio files uploaded by users remain exclusively inside local device memory (RAM) and are never transmitted to remote servers.

---

## 2. Technical Architecture & Privacy

### 2.1 Web Audio DSP Pipeline
- **API**: W3C Web Audio API (`AudioContext`, `AudioBufferSourceNode`, `GainNode`, `StereoPannerNode`, `ScriptProcessorNode` / `AudioWorklet`).
- **Sample Rates**: Native hardware support up to 48 kHz / 32-bit float internal audio processing.
- **Output Standards**: Uncompressed 16-bit PCM / 48 kHz stereo WAV export.
- **Click-Free Transitions**: Amplitude envelopes implement linear and exponential ramps (40ms ramp-in and ramp-out) on play/pause/stop events to eliminate speaker pop and transient clicks.

### 2.2 Client-Side Data & Privacy Model
- **Audio Files**: 0 cloud uploads. Audio file processing is strictly performed locally in the user's browser memory.
- **Preset Storage**: User-created tone mixtures and soundscape presets are saved in browser IndexedDB.
- **Portability**: Presets can be exported as standard JSON files and re-imported across browsers.
- **Authentication**: The web application uses Firebase Authentication for account management. Account metadata is isolated from local audio files.

---

## 3. Acoustic Tools & Signal Processing

### 3.1 432 Hz Song Converter
- **Purpose**: Converts audio recorded in standard concert pitch (A4 = 440 Hz) to Verdi tuning (A4 = 432 Hz).
- **Pitch Ratio**: 
  $$\text{Ratio} = \frac{432}{440} \approx 0.981818\dots$$
- **Cents Formula**:
  $$\Delta \text{Cents} = 1200 \times \log_2\left(\frac{432}{440}\right) \approx -31.767 \text{ cents}$$
- **Acoustic Characteristics**: Lowering standard tuning by approximately 31.8 cents creates a warmer, slightly deeper acoustic character without altering melodic relationships.
- **Processing Time**: Typically processed in 3 to 10 seconds depending on file duration and client hardware.
- **Supported Formats**: Supported uncompressed/lossless audio formats (WAV, FLAC) with uncompressed WAV download.

### 3.2 Frequency Laboratory
- **Oscillator Type**: High-purity mathematical sine wave synthesis.
- **Tuning Precision**: 0.01 Hz frequency adjustment.
- **Key Frequencies**:
  - **432.00 Hz**: Natural mathematical harmonic tuning (Verdi reference pitch).
  - **528.00 Hz**: Solfeggio "transformation" tone, harmonic resonant frequency.
  - **7.83 Hz**: Fundamental Schumann resonance frequency (Earth-ionosphere resonant cavity).
- **Modulation**: Optional amplitude modulation (AM) and binaural stereophonic differential modulation.

### 3.3 Guided Soundscapes & Noise Synthesis
- **Binaural Brown Noise**: Filtered with a $-6 \text{ dB/octave}$ ($1/f^2$) power spectral density slope. Provides warm, deep acoustic masking to drown out environmental distractions and silence mental chatter.
- **Pink Noise**: Filtered with a $-3 \text{ dB/octave}$ ($1/f$) spectral slope, providing equal energy per octave.
- **Stereo Binaural Separation**: Transmits slightly detuned frequencies independently to the left and right ears, allowing the auditory cortex to perceive a phantom difference frequency (binaural beat).

---

## 4. Responsible Listening & Safety Guidelines
- **Headphone Requirement**: Binaural beats strictly require stereo headphones to maintain channel isolation. Standard loudspeakers mix stereo channels in ambient air, reducing or canceling the binaural perception.
- **Hearing Safety**: Pure sinusoidal tones carry concentrated acoustic energy. Users are advised to begin listening at 20–30% volume and adjust to comfortable levels.
- **Non-Medical Statement**: HEARTz is an acoustic tool for focus, sound design, and personal relaxation. It is not a medical device and makes no diagnostic, therapeutic, or medical claims.

---

## 5. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### What makes 432 Hz different from standard 440 Hz?
A4 = 440 Hz is the modern ISO 16 concert pitch standard adopted internationally in the 20th century. A4 = 432 Hz (often called Verdi tuning or scientific pitch) places middle A slightly lower by approximately 31.8 cents. Many listeners and musicians find the lower tuning softer, warmer, and less fatiguing during prolonged work or meditation sessions.

### Are user audio files uploaded to any server?
No. HEARTz operates on a zero-upload privacy architecture. Decoding, resampling, and WAV encoding occur directly in the browser's local RAM. Files never leave the user's computer or mobile device.

### Can I export the retuned audio?
Yes. Converted files can be exported directly as lossless, uncompressed 16-bit / 48 kHz WAV files for offline listening in any standard media player.

### Does HEARTz require a paid subscription?
HEARTz features free browser-based access with optional account registration for saving personalized library presets.
